quote: We do both. So we have multiple different options, depending on what what's gonna be the best fit for you or what you, what you prefer.
stewart_read: This is a soft version of scope creep — the rep answers a financing-mechanism question with a vague generality rather than either a concrete fact or a clean redirect to the specialist. It's not wrong content, but it's also not the universal escape hatch language the schema recommends.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep genuinely didn't know the distinction yet and was buying time. Strategic read is not well supported here since the rep later admits at 02:00 he doesn't know the specifics — so this earlier answer reads as improvised rather than deliberate deferral.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to use the schema's escape hatch verbatim-in-spirit ('that's exactly what the specialist walks you through') the first time a financing-mechanism question comes up, rather than a vague 'we do both' that invites two more rounds of the same question.

quote: Yeah. I'm not quite too sure about all the specifics on on on what works with either one, because, again, my job is just kinda get this design built out, and then, we'll have someone we would get to kinda go over that in a little bit more detail.
stewart_read: This is the 'admit and recover with transparency' variant of knowledge-gap handling — the rep openly says he doesn't know the PPA-vs-loan differences and correctly routes it to the specialist. This is the right move, arriving one exchange later than it should have.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this as the correct pattern — the manager should note the honesty is good, but coach the rep to lead with this line at 01:05 instead of the vaguer 'we do both' answer.

quote: So what got what got me, what caught my attention under your ad is, it says solar, no cost, and you get a, Tesla Powerwall, and stuff like that.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers unprompted interest in the Powerwall battery specifically — a cross-sell-adjacent signal the rep could anchor on. Rep files it into notes but never reflects it back as a hook for the appointment.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to name the Powerwall interest explicitly when setting the appointment (e.g., tying the button-up to 'the specialist will walk through the battery option you asked about') to create forward-pulling curiosity rather than silently logging it.

quote: My energy bill is not very large, but the delivery fees are the ones that are, you know, a little bit upsetting.
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a textbook villain-reframe opportunity — he's already frustrated at a specific cost component. The rep never flips this into 'that delivery fee is exactly what solar takes off the table' language; the moment passes into general bill-collection instead.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read considered: rep might be deliberately staying neutral to avoid over-selling before the design exists. But the rep's own scope-discipline elsewhere (holding financing questions for the specialist) suggests this was simply not recognized as a flip opportunity, not a deliberate hold.
coaching_implication: Point to this exact line in the 1-on-1 as a missed inversion — the customer basically wrote the rep's rebuttal for him ('delivery fees are what's upsetting'), and a short reflection ('that delivery fee is the piece solar can't touch under your current setup — that's worth the specialist showing you') would have created curiosity without any invented numbers.

quote: Unfortunately, we don't have anybody in the area that could give you a phone call. It would just be, again, an in person appointment.
stewart_read: This isn't the in-person-vs-phone protocol failing — that's a legitimate operational hold. The real miss is adjacent: the customer explicitly cited spouse-scheduling conflict as the reason for the phone request ('my wife and I... hard to get us both at the same time'), which is a spouse-coordination signal the rep never picks up or resolves before locking a single-attendee 5PM slot.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep simply didn't register the spouse-availability detail as separate from the phone-format request. This is the better-supported read — the rep responds only to the format request, not the underlying scheduling-conflict rationale.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to separate 'format preference' from 'who needs to attend' — when a customer says both spouses are hard to catch at home together, that's the moment to ask directly whether the wife can be present Tuesday at 5, not just book the slot and move on.

quote: Are you able to email me the sign and, like, the cost and everything before that the representative would show up? I wouldn't be able to. I don't have access to anything like that. So, I can maybe request it, but I'm not I'm I don't know for sure what their what their policy is behind that. So I can definitely ask for you, but they'll have everything ready.
stewart_read: This is a held_line_with_improvisation case per the schema's own deviation grading — the rep doesn't cave and doesn't promise to send the proposal, but he also doesn't cite the firm 'we don't email proposals' policy; instead he hedges with 'I can maybe request it... I don't know for sure what their policy is.' The outcome (no proposal sent) matches the hard rule, but the framing signals uncertainty rather than the confident script line.
coaching_implication: The outcome was fine, but coach the rep to replace the hedge with the confident version: proposals aren't emailed because they need full walkthrough — same result, more authority, no implied policy confusion.

quote: And then, is there anybody else in the title of the home with you, or is it just you? Yeah. It'll be my wife too.
stewart_read: Co-owner is identified cleanly at verify stage, but never revisited at booking — the appointment is locked at Tuesday 5PM with no mention of whether the wife will be present, despite the customer separately flagging that both spouses are hard to schedule together.
coaching_implication: This is the single biggest structural gap in the call — flag for the manager: co-owner named, never confirmed for the appointment, and the customer even explained why that's hard. This appointment is booked but fragile exactly the way protocols.spouse_decision warns against.
